source.public_versification_note: Public 25:1–18, 26:2–65, 27–28 and 29:1–39 align directly. Public 26:1 combines Hebrew 25:19 and 26:1, each bound separately in source_segments. Public 29:40 maps to Hebrew 30:1; public 30:1–16 maps to Hebrew 30:2–17. All 194 original records are hashed exactly for 193 public verses.

key_decisions.decision: Keeps male referent because the chapter distinguishes men and women; retains vow, oath and full spoken obligation.
Preserves youth and residence as conditions rather than applying the rule to every unmarried adult woman.
Retains same-day limit and divine forgiveness rather than removing the theological term; a note explains release from the obligation in context.
Chooses marriage with an existing obligation, noting the alternative already-married reading; preserves rash speech as a separate category.
Preserves the husband’s same-day veto, both speech categories and divine forgiveness without presenting the arrangement as gender-symmetrical.
Retains the distinct binding force of these women’s vows rather than extending a male relative’s veto to them.
Treats this as the case of vows made within marriage, with the alternative retrospective connection to verse 9 noted.
Keeps emphatic cancellation, same-day timing, full spoken scope and repeated cancellation/forgiveness clauses.
Retains self-affliction qualification and husband’s unequal authority without restricting the obligation only to fasting.
Retains after-hearing timing and transfer of guilt, with later-than-initial-silence context explained in a note rather than changing the condition silently.
Preserves relational and residence scope in the narrator’s conclusion; binds Hebrew 30:17.
